description: Na₄LiCl₅ is Caswellsilverite-like structured and crystallizes in the tetragonal I4/m space group. Na is bonded to six Cl atoms to form NaCl₆ octahedra that share  a cornercorner with one LiCl₆ octahedra, corners with five equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra, edges with three equivalent LiCl₆ octahedra, and edges with nine equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-5°. There are a spread of Na-Cl bond distances ranging from 2.74-2.84 Å. Li is bonded to six Cl atoms to form LiCl₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent LiCl₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra, and edges with twelve equivalent NaCl₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-1°. There are four shorter (2.63 Å) and two longer (2.76 Å) Li-Cl bond lengths. There are two inequivalent Cl sites. In the first Cl site, Cl is bonded to five equivalent Na and one Li atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ClNa₅Li octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-4°. In the second Cl site, Cl is bonded to four equivalent Na and two equivalent Li atoms to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing ClNa₄Li₂ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-3°.
